mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Strong to severe surface gusts remain possible, mainly northwest through north of Omaha, perhaps into the Omaha area, through 5-6 AM CDT. New thunderstorm development, including an evolving cluster or two, appears possible across central/southern Iowa through 6-8 AM, accompanied by a risk for severe hail and perhaps gradually increasing potential for strong to severe surface gusts. Trends will be monitored for the possibility of a downstream severe weather watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Likely due to the presence of substantive mid-level inhibition and weak low-level forcing for ascent, the initially intense cluster of storms has undergone notable weakening the past couple of hours. However, a notable 2-hourly surface pressure rise on the order of 5-6 mb, within the evolving cold pool across the O'Neil into Norfolk vicinity, has been maintained near/beneath the remnant MCV, and may continue to be accompanied by stronger surface gusts at least another hour or two, near/northwest through north of Omaha. Otherwise, the east-southeastward propagating convectively augmented perturbation has contributed to some southward suppression of the elevated mixed-layer plume, and the lower-level baroclinic zone along which the deeper boundary-layer moisture is concentrated. Forcing for ascent associated with low-level warm advection downstream of the perturbation is beginning to support some ongoing increase in thunderstorm development near/north of I-80 across central Iowa. Closer to a 20-40 kt west-southwesterly 850 mb jet axis, guidance suggests a further increase in thunderstorm development is probable through 11-13Z. Given potential inflow of seasonably moist air supportive of most unstable CAPE at least on the order of 2000+ J/kg, the evolution of another vigorous upscale growing cluster appears possible, eventually becoming accompanied by increasing risk for strong to severe surface gusts
